title: Debounce KEDA external scaler and stabilize probe-derived metrics to reduce false scale events
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: A capacity incident on 2026-01-17 exposed an autoscaling regression where the KEDA external scaler and HPA interacted poorly with noisy probe/read-rate signals. The result was repeated rapid scale-downs followed by cold-start spikes, elevated P95 latency, and increased token cost during recovery. This ticket documents root cause analysis, short-term mitigations applied during the incident, and the action plan to harden autoscaling decisions and probe aggregation logic.
timeline: 2026-01-17 02:58 UTC: Production alerts triggered - P95 latency above SLO for serving-runtime across us-west-2 cluster.
2026-01-17 03:04 UTC: Observed scale-downs from 40 -> 12 replicas in two waves within 90s; warm-pool occupancy at 0%; KV-cache miss spike correlates with cold starts.

2026-01-17 03:07 UTC: KEDA external scaler logs show transient drop in external metric 'inflight_requests_per_replica' due to 1-minute window with a spike exfoliation, no debounce in scaler decision path.

2026-01-17 03:12 UTC: Incident response applied quick mitigations: temporarily raised minReplicas to 20 for affected target and increased HPA stabilizationWindowSec to 120s for that HorizontalPodAutoscaler.
2026-01-17 04:10 UTC: Latency returned to baseline after warm-pool admission and pod startup completed. Incident declared mitigated.
2026-01-18 10:00 UTC: Post-incident RCA session with runtime, infra, observability, and product; decided to implement debounce + smoothing, probe aggregator, and warm-pool hedging.
2026-01-25 16:30 UTC: Load tests in staging with synthetic spike patterns executed to validate debounce and EWMA smoothing parameters.
2026-02-04 09:20 UTC: PRs opened for scaler debounce and probe aggregation; smoke tests passed in canary cluster (canary rollout started).
root_cause_summary: Two orthogonal signal issues amplified each other: (1) the KEDA external scaler used a short raw rate metric with no temporal debounce, so transient drops caused immediate scale-downs; (2) readiness/liveness probe flapping due to GC pauses and ephemeral network errors was being counted as a signal for HPA decisions in aggregated dashboards. The HPA scaleDown stabilizationWindowSec was configured to 30s in many targets, too short for our cold-start penalty. Combined these caused a feedback loop of scale-down -> cold start -> increased latency -> more errors.
remediation: Immediate: raised minReplicas and stabilized HPA for the impacted deployment, enabled warm-pool admission to maintain spare capacity, and disabled overly-aggressive scale-to-zero runbooks for the affected service tier. Medium term: implement a debounce layer in the KEDA scaler decision path, add EWMA smoothing of per-replica request-rate metric, add a probe-aggregator that ignores single-probe anomalies, and increase default HPA stabilizationWindowSec. Long term: introduce a simulation harness for autoscaler logic that runs historical traffic traces against proposed tuning changes to quantify cold-start cost and SLO regressions.
action_items: ENG-450321-A1: Implement scaler debounce middleware (hold scale decision until metric shows sustained change for configurable duration). Owner: Diego Morales. Due: 2026-02-10.
ENG-450321-A2: Add EWMA smoothing to external metrics pipeline for 'inflight_requests_per_replica' (alpha=0.15 default, configurable). Owner: Priya Shah. Due: 2026-02-08.

ENG-450321-A3: Deploy probe-aggregator that computes rolling agreement between readiness and liveness and ignores single-sample failures when readiness majority is healthy. Owner: Liang Chen. Due: 2026-02-14.
ENG-450321-A4: Increase HPA default scaleDown stabilizationWindowSec to 60s for model-serving workloads and document tradeoffs. Owner: Diego Morales. Due: 2026-02-06.
ENG-450321-A5: Implement warm-pool hedging configuration in Dedicated and Hosted profiles (reserve 5-10% capacity based on QPS percentile). Owner: SRE Team (oncall rotation). Due: 2026-02-20.
ENG-450321-A6: Build autoscaler simulation harness and run against Jan 2026 traffic trace; deliver report with recommended tuning parameters. Owner: Applied ML / Runtime. Due: 2026-03-01.

ENG-450321-A7: Create dashboards and alerts to detect 'rapid scale oscillation' (>=2 scale events in 90s) and 'cold-start cost spike' (KV cache miss + P95 latency). Owner: Observability Team. Due: 2026-02-04.
ENG-450321-A8: Update runbooks to include a 'retain-min-on-spike' emergency knob and guidance for when to temporarily increase minReplicas. Owner: Oncall Runbook Maintainer. Due: 2026-02-04.
ENG-450321-A9: Retro and postmortem review with product to evaluate SLA / cost tradeoffs for different warm-pool sizes. Owner: Product. Due: 2026-02-18.
ENG-450321-A10: Security review for new scaler middleware to ensure metrics pipeline auth and no credential leakage. Owner: Security (requested). Due: 2026-02-12.
Note: owners above are primary and may add sub-tasks; any change touching scaler contract must include compatibility test in e2e CI.
followup_checks: Add alert: RapidScaleOscillation (>=2 scale events for same HPA target within 90s) -> pager P1 to SRE and runtime lead.
Add dashboard tile: ScalerDecisionHeatmap showing raw metric, smoothed metric, and debounce state over time.
Run 7-day canary with new debounce and smoothing enabled on 10% of traffic and monitor cold-start cost and P95 latency.
Automated canary gate: block global rollout if cold-start cost increases >10% or P95 latency regression >5% over baseline.
Weekly review of warm-pool utilization metrics for first 6 weeks post-rollout.
Integrate simulation harness into PR pipeline so parameter changes run historical trace tests automatically.
